Main.SCPLib.solve! — Method

Solve non-convex OCP with SCvx* algorithm

Arguments

  • algo::SCvxStar: algorithm struct
  • prob::OptimalControlProblem: problem struct
  • x_ref: reference state history, size nx-by-N
  • u_ref: reference control history, size nu-by-N-1
  • maxiter::Int: maximum number of iterations
  • tol_feas::Float64: feasibility tolerance
  • tol_opt::Float64: optimality tolerance
  • tol_J0::Real: objective tolerance
  • J_expected::Real: expected objective value
  • K_w::Real: initial penalty weight scaling factor
  • verbosity::Int: verbosity level
  • store_iterates::Bool: whether to store iterates
  • callback::Union{Nothing,Function}: called each iteration as callback(algo, solution, iteration, J0, χ)
  • warmstart_primal::Bool: whether to warmstart primal variables
  • warmstart_dual::Bool: whether to warmstart dual variables
  • tol_ΔL::Float64: relative tolerance on the predicted reduction; |ΔL| ≤ ε with ε = min(tol_ΔL * max(1,|J_ref|), tol_opt) is treated as zero (no model decrease); a negative tol_opt leaves ε uncapped and disables the stationarity-based exits (:Optimal from a null step, :InfeasibleStationary)
  • tol_ΔL_null::Float64: relative bound on how negative ΔL may be in a null step; with the trust-region inactive, ΔL < -ε_null, ε_null = max(ε, tol_ΔL_null * max(1,|J_ref|), tol_opt), is treated as a failed subproblem solve / inconsistent model and rejected instead of certifying the reference as stationary
  • max_null_steps::Int: number of consecutive null steps at an infeasible reference after which :InfeasibleStationary is returned

Step classification

  • If the initial guess violates the convex constraints of the model, the first step is a restoration step: it is accepted without a ratio test and the trust-region is kept.
  • If ΔL > ε, the usual ratio test ρ = ΔJ/ΔL is applied.
  • If -ε_null ≤ ΔL ≤ ε and the trust-region is inactive, the reference is a stationary point of the subproblem (null step): it is returned as :Optimal if feasible, otherwise the multipliers and penalty weight are updated at the reference. A candidate much worse than the reference (ΔL < -ε_null, see tol_ΔL_null) is rejected instead.
  • If |ΔL| ≤ ε with the trust-region active, the predicted decrease is unresolved at this trust-region size: the reference is kept and the trust-region expands.
  • If ΔL < -ε with the trust-region active, the step is rejected and the trust-region shrinks.

The returned solution (and solution.info, and the callback arguments) always describes the current iterate: the candidate of an accepted step, otherwise the reference. A rejected candidate is never returned (except when it already satisfies J0 ≤ tol_J0 and χ ≤ tol_feas).

Termination status

  • :Optimal: an accepted step that is not bounded by the trust-region has |ΔJ| ≤ tol_opt and χ ≤ tol_feas; or the reference is a feasible stationary point of the subproblem; or J0 ≤ tol_J0 with χ ≤ tol_feas
  • :Stalled / :Feasible: a step is rejected while the trust-region is already at its lower bound, so the subproblem cannot change; the last accepted reference is returned, with status :Feasible if it satisfies χ ≤ tol_feas and :Stalled otherwise
  • :InfeasibleStationary: max_null_steps consecutive null steps at a reference that violates the non-convex constraints (the multiplier and penalty updates cannot move it)
  • :CPFailed, :Feasible, :MaxIterReached: as before

Main.SCPLib.SCvxStar — Type

SCvx* algorithm

Arguments

  • nx::Int: number of states
  • N::Int: number of time steps
  • ng::Int: number of non-convex equality constraints
  • nh::Int: number of non-convex inequality constraints
  • Δ0::Float64: initial trust-region size
  • w0::Float64: initial penalty weight
  • rhos::Tuple{Real,Real,Real}: trust-region acceptance thresholds
  • alphas::Tuple{Real,Real}: trust-region size update factors
  • Δ_bounds::Tuple{Float64,Float64}: trust-region size bounds
  • gamma::Float64: stationarity tolerance update factor
  • beta::Float64: penalty weight update factor
  • w_max::Float64: maximum penalty weight
  • l1_penalty::Bool: whether to append an l1 penalty term √w‖·‖₁ to the augmented Lagrangian
  • nu::Union{Nothing,Int}: number of controls (optional; only used to build the control trust-region at construction, otherwise it is built from the problem at the first solve)
  • Δ0_u: initial control trust-region size (used if use_trustregion_control = true)
  • use_trustregion_control::Bool: whether to also impose a trust-region on the controls u
  • shooting_method::Symbol: :multiple or :forwardbackward
Trust-region on the controls

By default (use_trustregion_control = false) the trust-region only bounds the states x. The convergence theory of SCvx* (Oguri 2023) and SCvx (Mao et al. 2018) assumes a trust-region on all decision variables, which is what makes the linearization error (and hence the ratio test) vanish as Δ → 0. When the dynamics or the non-convex constraints are nonlinear in u (state-dependent control matrix, time-dilation control for free final time, nonlinear g/h in u), set use_trustregion_control = true; otherwise the algorithm may stall with repeated rejections or accept poorly modelled steps in u.

Main.SCPLib.add_l1_slacks! — Method
add_l1_slacks!(algo::SCvx, prob::OptimalControlProblem)

Create the epigraph variables t ≥ ‖ξ_dyn‖₁, t ≥ ‖ξ‖₁, t ≥ ‖ζ‖₁ of the exact penalty. These do not depend on the reference, so they are created once per solve and reused at every iteration (only the objective is rebuilt).

Main.SCPLib.solve! — Method

Solve non-convex OCP with SCvx algorithm

Keyword arguments

  • callback::Union{Nothing,Function}: called each iteration as callback(algo, solution, iteration, J0, χ)
  • tol_ΔL::Float64: relative tolerance on the predicted reduction; |ΔL| ≤ ε with ε = min(tol_ΔL * max(1,|J_ref|), tol_opt) is treated as zero (no model decrease); a negative tol_opt leaves ε uncapped and disables the stationarity-based exits (:Optimal from a null step, :InfeasibleStationary)
  • tol_ΔL_null::Float64: relative bound on how negative ΔL may be in a null step; with the trust-region inactive, ΔL < -ε_null, ε_null = max(ε, tol_ΔL_null * max(1,|J_ref|), tol_opt), is treated as a failed subproblem solve / inconsistent model and rejected instead of certifying the reference as stationary

Step classification and termination

Steps are classified as in solve!(::SCvxStar, ...) (restoration step from a convex-infeasible initial guess, ratio test, null step, rejection); as there, the returned solution describes the current iterate, so a rejected candidate is never returned. Termination statuses:

  • :Optimal: an accepted step that is not bounded by the trust-region has |ΔJ| ≤ tol_opt and χ ≤ tol_feas; or the reference is a feasible stationary point of the subproblem; or J0 ≤ tol_J0 with χ ≤ tol_feas
  • :InfeasibleStationary: the reference is a stationary point of the penalized problem (ΔL ≈ 0) but violates the non-convex constraints (Mao et al. 2018); increase w
  • :Stalled / :Feasible: a step is rejected while the trust-region is already at its lower bound, so the subproblem cannot change; the last accepted reference is returned, with status :Feasible if it satisfies χ ≤ tol_feas and :Stalled otherwise
  • :CPFailed, :Feasible, :MaxIterReached

Prox-linear method

Main.SCPLib.add_proxlinear_slacks! — Method
add_proxlinear_slacks!(algo::ProxLinear, prob::OptimalControlProblem)

Create the slack variables of the prox-linear subproblem: the l1 epigraph of the dynamics defects ϵ_noncvx_dyn ≥ |ξ_dyn|, the l1 epigraph of the non-convex equality constraints ϵ_noncvx_g ≥ ‖ξ‖₁, and the proximal-term epigraph variable ϵ_proximal. The first two do not depend on the reference, so they are created once per solve and reused; the second-order cone constraint defining ϵ_proximal ≥ ‖Z - Z_ref‖₂ is replaced at each iteration.

Main.SCPLib.ProxLinear — Type

Prox-linear algorithm

The weights are defined such that the penalized objective of the subproblems are:

\[L(Z) + w_ep * ||G(Z) + ∇G(Z_ref)*(Z - Z_ref)||_1 + w_prox/2 * ||Z - Z_ref||_2^2\]

where L(Z) is the original objective function, G(Z) are the non-convex constraints.

Arguments

  • w_ep::Float64: exact penalty term weight
  • w_prox::Float64: proximal term weight
  • proximal_u::Bool: whether to enforce proximal constraint on u

Main.SCPLib.solve! — Method

Solve non-convex OCP with fixed trust-region-weight SCP Algorithm

This algorithm employs a fixed trust-region & accepts every convex subproblem step. Artificial infeasibility is avoided by introducing slack variables for nonlinear constraints that are penalized quadratically with a fixed weight.

Arguments

  • algo::FixedTRWSCP: algorithm struct
  • prob::OptimalControlProblem: problem struct
  • x_ref: reference state history, size nx-by-N
  • u_ref: reference control history, size nu-by-N-1
  • maxiter::Int: maximum number of iterations
  • tol_feas::Float64: feasibility tolerance
  • tol_opt::Float64: optimality tolerance
  • tol_J0::Real: objective tolerance
  • verbosity::Int: verbosity level
  • store_iterates::Bool: whether to store iterates
  • callback::Union{Nothing,Function}: called each iteration as callback(algo, solution, iteration, J0, χ)

Trust regions

Main.SCPLib.clamp_trust_region! — Method
clamp_trust_region!(algo::SCPAlgorithm)

Clamp the trust-region radii into algo.Δ_bounds (e.g. an initial Δ0 below Δ_min, where the subproblem solution is below the solver accuracy and the trust-region tests are meaningless). NaN radii (unused slots of mixed problems) stay NaN.

source
Main.SCPLib.classify_step — Method
classify_step(ΔJ, ΔL, J_ref, ref_feasible, ref_is_initial_guess, tr_active;
              tol_ΔL = 1e-8, tol_abs = Inf, tol_ΔL_null = 1e-3)

Classify a trust-region step from the actual (ΔJ) and predicted (ΔL) merit reductions. Returns (rho, kind), where rho = ΔJ/ΔL (or NaN if ΔL == 0) and kind is one of:

  • :restoration: the reference does not satisfy the convex constraints (ref_feasible = false, or ΔL < -ε while the reference is still the initial guess, which indicates it: for a convex-feasible z̄ and a consistent model, L(z̄) = J(z̄) and ΔL ≥ 0). The ratio is meaningless; the step is accepted without a ratio test.
  • :ratio: ΔL > ε; the regular ratio test applies to rho.
  • :stationary: -ε_null ≤ ΔL ≤ ε and the trust-region is inactive at the candidate (null step). The reference is feasible for its own subproblem with L(z̄) = J(z̄), so the subproblem cannot improve on it by more than ε (a slightly negative ΔL only means the solver returned a point marginally worse than z̄, i.e. z̄ is optimal to within the solver accuracy); since the trust-region is inactive, z̄ is a stationary point of the penalized problem. The negative side is bounded by ε_null = max(ε, tol_ΔL_null * max(1, |J_ref|), tol_abs) (tol_abs only if it is a positive finite number). The solver noise in ΔL can exceed ε and the optimality tolerance: z̄ satisfies the convex constraints only to the solver accuracy, and the penalty weight amplifies the correction the subproblem has to make (ΔL ≈ -3e-5 with J ≈ 0.2 has been observed both at w = 1e3 and at w ≈ 3e12). A candidate worse than z̄ by more than ε_null is not noise but a failed solve or an inconsistent model.
  • :unresolved: |ΔL| ≤ ε while the step is bounded by the trust-region: the predicted decrease is below resolution because the trust-region is too small to tell. The reference is kept and the trust-region is expanded (shrinking would only make ΔL smaller).
  • :reject: ΔL < -ε while the step is bounded by the trust-region, or ΔL < -ε_null while it is not (inconsistent model or failed subproblem solve); the trust-region is shrunk.

The threshold is ε = min(tol_ΔL * max(1, |J_ref|), tol_abs): relative to the merit to account for solver accuracy, but never above tol_abs (the optimality tolerance), so that a constant offset in the objective cannot hide a decrease the stopping test would care about. A non-positive tol_abs (convergence test disabled) leaves ε uncapped.

Check whether (x_ref, u_ref) satisfies the convex constraints of prob.model that involve only x and u (constraints that involve other variables are skipped). Must be called before the linearized/trust-region constraints are added to the model. Returns true if the check cannot be carried out.

Main.SCPLib.trust_region_active — Method
trust_region_active(algo, x, u, x_ref, u_ref; rtol = 1e-3, atol = 1e-8)

Whether the convex subproblem solution (x,u) lies on the boundary of the trust-region around (x_ref,u_ref), i.e. some component satisfies |x - x_ref| ≥ max((1 - rtol) Δ - atol, Δ/2) (atol accounts for the absolute accuracy of interior-point solutions at small Δ). When the trust-region is inactive, the subproblem solution is the minimizer of the convex model over the convex feasible set, so small model/merit changes indicate stationarity; when it is active, they may only reflect a small trust-region.

Main.SCPLib.trust_region_at_lower_bound — Method
trust_region_at_lower_bound(algo::SCPAlgorithm)

True when every trust-region radius (state, and control if used) is already at its lower bound Δ_bounds[1], so a rejected step cannot shrink the subproblem any further. NaN radii (unused slots of mixed problems) are ignored.

source
Main.SCPLib.update_trust_region! — Method
update_trust_region!(algo::SCPAlgorithm, rho_i::Float64)

Update trust-region size Δ from the ratio rho_i: shrink if rho_i < rhos[2], expand if rho_i >= rhos[3], keep otherwise. NaN radii are left unchanged. Returns true if the trust-region size actually changed.

source
Main.SCPLib.update_trust_region! — Method
update_trust_region!(algo::SCPAlgorithm, action::Symbol)

Apply a trust-region update action ∈ (:shrink, :expand, :keep) to algo.tr (and to algo.tr_u when the control trust-region is used), clamped to algo.Δ_bounds. NaN radii are left unchanged. Returns true if the trust-region size actually changed.
